mainTopic: Who is פטור when a בית דין rules in error, what wording makes a real הוראה, and the man who mixed up חלב with שומן under the court's ruling.
overview: The משנה opens מסכת הוריות. If a בית דין mistakenly permits something the Torah forbids, an ordinary יחיד who acts on that ruling by mistake is פטור, because he relied on the בית דין. A judge who knew they were wrong, or a תלמיד who is ראוי להוראה, is חייב, because he really relied on himself. The גמרא asks what wording makes a ruling count. In one version שמואל requires "you are permitted," and רב דימי מנהרדעא requires "you are permitted to do it." In a second version the opinions are switched. In both versions, אביי, רבי אבא and רבינא use the same three sources to show that a real הוראה tells people to act. The גמרא then asks why the משנה says 'שוגג', and רבא has two versions about a man who mixed up חלב with שומן after the court permitted חלב. רבא's attempted proofs from the משנה are rejected, and the case turns out to be a dispute between רב (פטור) and רבי יוחנן (חייב). רב פפא defends רבי יוחנן with the rule of שב מידיעתו, and רבא adds that even רב agrees this man does not count toward the majority of the community. Finally the גמרא asks why the משנה lists its cases in the order it does, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: An individual who follows the court's mistaken ruling is exempt
steps.stepSummary: If a בית דין wrongly permits a Torah prohibition and a יחיד acts on it by accident, he is פטור from a קרבן. It does not matter whether the judges did it with him, before him, or not at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the court ruled that one may break any Torah מצוה, and an ordinary person accidentally acted on their ruling, he is exempt. This is true whether the judges did it together with him, did it before him, or did not do it at all. The reason is that he relied on the court.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens the מסכת with its first case: a regular person who acts on a mistaken ruling of the בית דין is פטור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally someone who sins בשוגג brings a קרבן. Here he is פטור because he was relying on the בית דין's ruling. The three cases (with them, after them, without them) show that what the judges themselves did makes no difference. Only the person's reliance on the בית דין matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
They ruled, gave an official halachic ruling
An individual, as opposed to the community
Unintentionally, by mistake
Exempt, here from bringing a קרבן
He relied on, hung his action on

phrases.english: MISHNA: If the court ruled
to transgress one
of all the מצוות stated in the Torah,
and the individual went and did it
unwittingly, based on their word,
whether they did it and he did it with them,
or they did it and he did it after them,
or they did not do it and he did it, he is exempt,
because he relied on the court.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הוֹרוּ בֵּית דִּין לַעֲבוֹר עַל אַחַת מִכׇּל מִצְוֹת הָאֲמוּרוֹת בַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening of the מסכת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A יחיד who acts בשוגג on a mistaken ruling of the בית דין is פטור, because he relied on the בית דין.

steps.title: A judge who knew the truth, or a qualified student, is liable
steps.stepSummary: If one of the judges knew the ruling was wrong, or a תלמיד who is ראוי להוראה acted on it, he is חייב in all three cases. He did not truly rely on the בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the court ruled, and one of the judges knew they made a mistake, or a student qualified to give rulings knew, and he still went and acted on their ruling, he is liable. This is true whether the judges did it with him, before him, or not at all, because he did not rely on the court.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite case: someone who knows enough to see the mistake is חייב even though he followed the בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The action is the same as in step 1, but the person is different. Since this person knew, or was able to know, that the ruling was wrong, his action came from his own mistake and not from reliance on the בית דין. So he is חייב a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: They erred
A student
Qualified to issue halachic rulings
Liable, here to bring a קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think he is חייב because he disobeyed the בית דין. He actually followed them. He is חייב because, knowing better, he could not truly rely on them.

phrases.aramaic: הוֹרוּ בֵּית דִּין, וְיָדַע אֶחָד מֵהֶן שֶׁטָּעוּ,
phrases.english: If the court ruled, and one of them knew that they erred,
or a student who is fit to issue rulings,
and he went and acted on their word,
whether they did it and he did it with them,
or they did it and he did it after them,
or they did not do it and he did it,
this one is liable,
because he did not rely on the court.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹרוּ בֵּית דִּין, וְיָדַע אֶחָד מֵהֶן שֶׁטָּעוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasting case: the same action, but done by a knowledgeable person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A judge who knew of the error, or a תלמיד who is ראוי להוראה, is חייב even when he acted on the ruling, since he did not rely on the בית דין.

steps.title: The general rule: relying on yourself or on the court
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sums up both cases. Whoever relies on himself is חייב, and whoever relies on the בית דין is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: whoever relies on himself is liable, and whoever relies on the court is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה wraps up the two cases with one clear principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding question is whose judgment the person was really following. If the action rests on the בית דין, he is פטור. If it rests on his own understanding, he is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general principle
One who relies on himself

steps.whatToRemember: Exemption depends on real reliance on the בית דין. A יחיד who relied on them is פטור. Someone qualified who knew better is חייב.

phrases.english: This is the principle:
one who relies on himself is liable,
and one who relies on the court is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הַכְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Summarizes steps 1 and 2 in one rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Liability depends on whether one relied on oneself or on the בית דין.

steps.title: שמואל: the court must say 'You are permitted'
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the בית דין is only חייב for a mistaken ruling once they actually tell people "you are permitted."
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: the court is never liable until they tell the people, "You are permitted."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by defining what counts as a real ruling of the בית דין: שמואל requires the words "you are permitted."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה spoke of a בית דין that "ruled," and שמואל sets the minimum wording for that. Only once they say "you are permitted" is the בית דין חייב for its mistaken ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
Never, in any case
You are permitted

phrases.english: GEMARA: Shmuel said:
The court is never liable
phrases.notes: Liable here means liable to bring the special קרבן for a mistaken ruling.

phrases.english: until they say to them: "You are permitted."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לְעוֹלָם אֵין בֵּית דִּין חַיָּיבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the word הוֹרוּ from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בית דין is חייב only after saying "you are permitted."

steps.title: רב דימי: they must say 'You are permitted to do it'
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי מנהרדעא requires more: the בית דין must say "you are permitted to do it."
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי מנהרדעא said: only once they tell them, "You are permitted to do it."
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a stricter definition of what makes the ruling count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב דימי, "you are permitted" alone is not enough. The בית דין has to add "to do it," which clearly tells people to act.

keyTerms.meaning: To do, to act
Neharde'a, a Torah center in בבל

phrases.english: Rav Dimi from Neharde'a said:
Not until they say to them:
"You are permitted to do it."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב דִּימִי מִנְּהַרְדְּעָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a requirement beyond שמואל's wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בית דין is חייב only after saying "you are permitted to do it."

steps.title: Why does רב דימי need the extra words?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב דימי's stricter wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by asking why רב דימי needs the words "to do it."
steps.deeperAnalysis: "You are permitted" already sounds like a ruling. So the גמרא wants to know what is missing without the word "to do it."

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב דימי requires "to do it" in addition to "you are permitted."

steps.title: Without 'to do it' the ruling is incomplete
steps.stepSummary: Without the words "to do it," the הוראה is not finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the ruling is not complete.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that "you are permitted" alone is not yet a finished ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A finished הוראה must be a practical instruction to act. Saying only "permitted" could be an opinion in theory, so the בית דין is not yet held responsible for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Was completed
A halachic ruling

phrases.english: Because the ruling was not completed.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא נִגְמְרָה הוֹרָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Without "to do it," the הוראה is not complete.

steps.title: אביי supports רב דימי from the rebellious elder
steps.stepSummary: אביי shows that the משנה about the זקן ממרא also separates teaching from ruling to act, which supports רב דימי.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We also learned this in a משנה. If he went back to his city and taught the way he used to teach, he is exempt. If he ruled for people to act, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings proof from another משנה that a ruling only counts when it tells people to act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The זקן ממרא is only חייב when he tells people to act on his ruling, not when he just teaches it. The same idea fits רב דימי: a ruling is complete only with "to do it."

keyTerms.meaning: We also learned this in a משנה
A rebellious elder who rules against the סנהדרין
He ruled that people should act

steps.whatToRemember: A real הוראה is a practical instruction to act. Teaching an opinion is not enough, and this is what makes the בית דין, or a זקן ממרא, חייב.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא:
phrases.english: Abaye said: We too have learned this:
If he returned to his city and taught
phrases.notes: This is from the משנה about the זקן ממרא (סנהדרין 86b), who disagreed with the סנהדרין.

phrases.english: and taught the way he used to teach, he is exempt,
but if he ruled for people to act, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רב דימי's view and reason.
steps.raayaObject: רב דימי's view that a ruling is complete only when it says "to do it."
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of the זקן ממרא in סנהדרין: teaching makes him פטור, ruling to act makes him חייב.

steps.title: רבי אבא's proof from the woman who was allowed to remarry
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא brings a משנה from יבמות. The בית דין permitted a woman only to marry, so if she acted immorally she is fully responsible herself. This supports רב דימי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: We also learned this in a משנה. If בית דין told a woman she may marry, and she went and acted immorally, she must bring a קרבן. This is because they only allowed her to marry.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא adds a second proof for רב דימי, from a משנה about a woman whom בית דין permitted to remarry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בית דין's permission covered only one specific action: getting married. Anything else she did was her own doing, so the court's ruling does not protect her. This shows that a הוראה is tied to a specific action, which is exactly רב דימי's point.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it (in a משנה): an opening line for bringing a supporting source
They ruled or instructed
To get married
She acted corruptly (had forbidden relations)
An offering brought for an accidental sin

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said,
We too have also learned it:
If the court instructed her to marry,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in יבמות 87b.

phrases.english: and she went and acted corruptly,
phrases.notes: She had forbidden relations outside of marriage, which the court never allowed.

phrases.english: she is liable to bring an offering,
since they permitted her only to marry.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second proof for רב דימי, following אביי's proof in step 8
steps.raayaObject: רב דימי's view that a הוראה must point to a specific action
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in יבמות 87b: the court permitted her only to marry

steps.title: רבינא's proof from the opening words of our משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבינא points out that our own משנה says the בית דין 'ruled to transgress,' so the ruling must be about doing something.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: We also learned this in our משנה: 'בית דין ruled to transgress one of the מצוות in the Torah.' Nothing more needs to be said.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings a third proof for רב דימי, straight from the first line of our own משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not just say 'they ruled'; it says they ruled 'to transgress,' which is an action. So the case in the משנה is a ruling that tells people to act, as רב דימי requires.

keyTerms.meaning: To transgress, to violate
The מצוות stated in the Torah
Nothing more (needs to be said)

phrases.english: Ravina said,
We too have also learned it:
"If the court ruled to transgress
phrases.notes: These are the opening words of our own משנה.

phrases.aramaic: עַל אַחַת מִכׇּל מִצְוֹת הָאֲמוּרוֹת בַּתּוֹרָה״,
phrases.english: one of all the מצוות stated in the Torah,"
nothing more [is needed].

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third proof for רב דימי, this time from the wording of our own משנה
steps.raayaObject: רב דימי's view that a הוראה must include 'to do it'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The opening line of our משנה: 'הורו בית דין לעבור'
steps.whatToRemember: In the first version, three proofs (אביי, רבי אבא, רבינא) all support רב דימי: a real הוראה tells people to act.

steps.title: A second version: שמואל requires 'to do it'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a different version of the מחלוקת. Now it is שמואל who says the בית דין is only חייב once they say 'you are permitted to do it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it this way: שמואל said, the בית דין is not חייב until they tell people, 'You are permitted to do it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second version of the same מחלוקת, with the opinions switched. Here שמואל holds the stricter wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, שמואל was satisfied with 'you are permitted.' In this version he requires 'you are permitted to do it,' which is what רב דימי said before. The topic stays the same; only who says what has changed.

keyTerms.meaning: They are liable (to bring a קרבן)
You are permitted to do it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two versions. In this second version, שמואל holds 'to do it' and רב דימי is the lenient one.

phrases.english: Some say [it this way]:
Shmuel said:
The court is not liable
until they say to them,
"You are permitted to do it."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the מחלוקת from steps 4-5 with the opinions reversed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, שמואל requires the words 'you are permitted to do it.'

steps.title: A second version: רב דימי says 'you are permitted' is enough
steps.stepSummary: In the reversed version, רב דימי says that even just 'you are permitted' already counts as a finished הוראה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי from נהרדעא said: Even if they just said 'You are permitted,' the הוראה is complete.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the second version of the מחלוקת. Here רב דימי takes the lenient side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רב דימי holds that permission alone, without 'to do it,' is a complete הוראה, so the בית דין is חייב. This sets up the next steps, where the same proofs used earlier for רב דימי will now be used against him.

keyTerms.meaning: Even
The ruling is complete

phrases.english: Rav Dimi from Neharde'a said:
Even [if they said] "You are permitted,"
the ruling is complete.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב דִּימִי מִנְּהַרְדְּעָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of the reversed מחלוקת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, רב דימי holds that 'you are permitted' alone is a completed הוראה.

steps.title: אביי challenges רב דימי from the זקן ממרא משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks: doesn't the משנה about the זקן ממרא separate just teaching from ruling to act? That goes against רב דימי's lenient view.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: But don't we learn otherwise? The משנה says: If he went back to his city and taught the way he used to teach, he is exempt. If he ruled for people to act, he is חייב.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי uses the same משנה from step 8, but now it serves as a challenge to רב דימי's view in the second version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה exempts the זקן ממרא when he only teaches, and makes him חייב only when he tells people to act. That shows a real הוראה needs 'to do it,' which goes against רב דימי's claim that 'you are permitted' is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn like this? A rhetorical challenge from a משנה
A rebellious elder who rules against the סנהדרין
He taught or instructed (as learning, not a ruling to act)
Exempt

phrases.english: Abaye said,
But don't we learn like this:
If he returned to his city,
phrases.notes: This is the זקן ממרא, the elder who disagreed with the סנהדרין.

phrases.english: and taught or instructed the way he had been teaching,
he is exempt;
if he ruled for people to act, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, וְהָא לָא תְּנַן הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב דימי's lenient view from step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי in the second version: 'you are permitted' is already a complete הוראה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה treats teaching and ruling to act differently, so a ruling without 'to do it' should not count as a full הוראה.

steps.title: רבי אבא challenges רב דימי from the woman who was allowed to remarry
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא repeats the משנה from יבמות, now as a challenge. The court's permission covered only marriage, which shows that a ruling is tied to a specific action.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: But don't we learn otherwise? If בית דין told a woman she may marry, and she went and acted immorally, she must bring a קרבן, because they only allowed her to marry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבי אבא's source from step 9, but in the second version it serves as a challenge to רב דימי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the court's permission covered only the act of marrying, a הוראה is clearly about a specific action. That goes against רב דימי, who says a general 'you are permitted' is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: They permitted
She is liable
Not ... except, meaning 'only'

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions use the same sources. In version one they support רב דימי ('to do it'); in version two they challenge רב דימי's lenient view. Either way, the sources show that a real הוראה tells people to act.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said,
But don't we learn like this:
If the court instructed her to marry,
and she went and acted corruptly,
she is liable to bring an offering,
since they permitted her only to marry.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא, וְהָא לָא תְּנַן הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רב דימי, using the same משנה from step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי in the second version: 'you are permitted' is already a complete הוראה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The court's permission was limited to one specific act, so a הוראה must point to an action. A general 'you are permitted' should not be enough.

steps.title: רבינא shows the משנה's wording does not fit רב דימי
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says that our משנה's own words, 'the בית דין ruled to transgress,' show that a ruling must be about doing an action. That defeats רב דימי's view in the reversed version.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: But our משנה was not taught that way. It says 'the בית דין ruled to transgress one of the מצוות of the Torah.' There is nothing more to say.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא uses the same words of the משנה from Step 10, but now he aims them at רב דימי in the reversed version. The משנה says the court ruled 'to transgress,' which means doing something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the reversed version, רב דימי said that just saying 'you are permitted' already counts as a full הוראה. The משנה's phrase 'ruled to transgress' points to a ruling about an actual action. So the משנה backs the stricter view, and רבינא declares the matter closed.

keyTerms.meaning: To transgress. The משנה's word that shows the ruling is about doing an act.
Nothing more. The case is closed.
But we did not learn it this way. This introduces a challenge from the wording of the משנה.

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same proof רבינא gave in Step 10, not a new idea. The only difference is that here it is aimed at רב דימי in the reversed version of the מחלוקת.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
But we did not learn it this way in the Mishnah:
The court ruled to transgress
one of all the מצוות
that are stated in the Torah,
Nothing more.
phrases.notes: In other words, the proof is so clear that nothing more needs to be said.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבינא והא לא תנן הכי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a final challenge from the משנה's wording, after the challenges of אביי and רבי אבא, against רב דימי in the reversed version.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's view in the reversed version, that 'you are permitted' alone is a full הוראה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה describes the ruling as 'to transgress,' which means permitting an action. Just teaching that something is allowed is not enough.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles that a הוראה which obligates the בית דין must be a ruling that permits actually doing the act.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need the word 'unwittingly'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה and asks why it says 'שוגג.' Anyone who relies on the court's ruling is obviously acting by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And the individual went and did it שוגג, on their word.' Let it just say 'and did it on their word.' Why do I need the word 'שוגג'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new phrase in the משנה and asks why one word seems to be extra. This question sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person acts 'on the word' of the בית דין, he thinks the act is allowed, so he is already acting by mistake. The word 'שוגג' looks like it adds nothing. The גמרא expects that it must teach some extra case.

keyTerms.meaning: An individual person, as opposed to the whole community.
Unwittingly. Doing a sin by mistake.
On their word. Relying on the court's ruling.
Why do I need it? This asks why a word in the source seems extra.

phrases.english: And the individual went
and did it unwittingly, on their word.
Let it teach: "and did it on their word."
Why do I need "unwittingly"?
phrases.notes: Relying on the court already means he thought it was allowed, so the word seems extra.

steps.triggerLanguage: וניתני ועשה על פיהם שוגג למה לי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the debate about what counts as a הוראה and begins explaining the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra case does the word 'שוגג' add to the משנה?

steps.title: רבא's first answer: 'unwittingly' includes the man who mixed up the fats
steps.stepSummary: רבא says 'שוגג' includes a man who mistook forbidden חלב for permitted שומן after the court permitted חלב. He is exempt. 'On their word' covers the man who truly relied on the ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: 'שוגג' comes to include this case. The בית דין ruled that חלב is permitted. The man mixed up חלב with שומן and ate it. He is exempt. 'On their word' means a man who really ate because of their word.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by giving each word its own case. 'On their word' covers the man who ate because of the ruling. 'שוגג' adds a man who ate it by an ordinary mix-up, while the ruling was in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mix-up man did not eat because of the ruling. He thought he was eating permitted שומן. Even so, the word 'שוגג' teaches that he is also exempt like the man who relied on the court, since the court's ruling was in place.

keyTerms.meaning: To include. To add an extra case.
Forbidden animal fat.
Permitted animal fat.
It got mixed up for him. He mistook one thing for another.
Really, literally.

phrases.english: Rava said:
"Unwittingly" comes to include
where the court ruled that forbidden fat is permitted,
and he mixed up forbidden fat with permitted fat,
and ate it: he is exempt.
"On their word" means really on their word.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבא שוגג לאתויי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16 by giving the word 'שוגג' its own extra case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each word of the משנה is given a separate case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'שוגג' seemed to add nothing beyond 'on their word.'
steps.terutzMaskana: 'שוגג' adds the man who mixed up חלב and שומן while the ruling was in place. He is also exempt.

steps.title: רבא's second version: the man who mixed up the fats is liable
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רבא reads 'שוגג על פיהם' as one phrase. Only someone who acted by mistake because of their word is exempt. The man who mixed up חלב with שומן is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רבא said: 'שוגג על פיהם' means that only when he acted by mistake because of their word is he exempt. But if he mixed up חלב with שומן and ate it, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of what רבא said, and it reaches the opposite result. Here the man who mixed up the fats must bring his own קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, 'שוגג' and 'על פיהם' are read together. The exemption is only for someone whose mistake came from the court's ruling. The man who mixed up the fats made his own private mistake, so the ruling does not protect him.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt. He does not need to bring his own קרבן.
Liable. He must bring his own קרבן חטאת.

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions describe exactly the same case. They do not disagree about the facts, only about the law: in the first version he is exempt, and in the second he is liable.

phrases.english: And some say that Rava said:
"Unwittingly" on their word:
phrases.notes: Here the two words are read together as one idea: a mistake caused by the ruling.

phrases.english: that is when he is exempt,
but if forbidden fat got mixed up for him with permitted fat
and he ate it, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: ואיכא דאמרי אמר רבא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רבא's answer, with the opposite ruling for the man who mixed up the fats.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The words 'שוגג על פיהם' are read together as one condition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Based on the first version, the man who mixed up the fats is exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exemption covers only a mistake caused by the court's ruling. The man who mixed up the fats is liable.

steps.title: What was obvious to רבא was a question for רמי בר חמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבא was sure about the mix-up case, one way or the other. But רמי בר חמא asked about it as an open question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Something that was obvious to רבא was a question for רמי בר חמא. רמי בר חמא asked: The בית דין ruled that חלב is permitted. The man mixed it up with שומן and ate it. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes the contrast between רבא, who was sure, and רמי בר חמא, who was unsure. It then sets up רמי בר חמא's question, which רבא tries to settle from the משנה in steps 20–23.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both versions, רבא gave a clear ruling: exempt in one version, liable in the other. רמי בר חמא saw the same case as a real doubt. Did the court's ruling still play a part, or did his private mix-up decide the outcome?

keyTerms.meaning: Obvious.
It is a question for him.
What is the law?

steps.whatToRemember: The word 'שוגג' in the משנה is about the man who mixed up חלב with שומן while the court's ruling was in place. רבא has two versions: exempt or liable. For רמי בר חמא, the same case was an open question.

phrases.english: A matter that was obvious to Rava
was a question for Rami bar Chama,
for Rami bar Chama asked:
If the court ruled that forbidden fat is permitted,
and it got mixed up for him with permitted fat, and he ate it,
what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: מילתא דפשיטא ליה לרבא קמיבעיא ליה לרמי בר חמא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts רבא's certainty in Steps 17 and 18 with רמי בר חמא's open question about the same case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a man who mixed up חלב with שומן, after the court permitted חלב, exempt or liable?

steps.title: רבא tries to prove from the extra words in the משנה that the mix-up case is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבא's statement is now presented as an attempted proof. The משנה's extra words 'שוגג על פיהם' seem to include the man who mixed up חלב with שומן and say he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come and hear. The משנה says, 'An individual went and acted by mistake on their word.' Why does it need both 'by mistake' and 'on their word'? Isn't it to include a case where the בית דין permitted חלב, and the man confused חלב with שומן and ate it? The משנה would be teaching that he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tries to settle רמי בר חמא's question from step 19 with a proof from our משנה. The next step rejects this proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is built on extra words. 'על פיהם' alone would cover the man who relied on the ruling, so 'שוגג' must add something more. רבא suggests it adds the man who mixed up חלב with שומן, and that he is also exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? This asks why the text has extra words.
To include (an extra case)
It got mixed up for him

phrases.english: Rava said: Come and hear:
An individual went and acted
by mistake, on their word, etc.
Why do I need 'by mistake, on their word'?
Is it not to include
a case where the court ruled that forbidden fat is permitted,
and he mixed up forbidden fat with permitted fat
and ate it, and he is exempt?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An attempt to resolve רמי בר חמא's question from step 19, using the extra word 'שוגג' that רבא explained in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: The man who mixed up חלב with שומן after the court permitted חלב is exempt.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra word 'שוגג' in the משנה's phrase 'שוגג על פיהם'.

steps.title: Rejection: the words may only exempt the one who truly relied on the ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes the proof away. 'שוגג על פיהם' might mean only the man who sinned because of the ruling is exempt, and the man who mixed things up is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps only someone who acted by mistake because of their word is exempt. But if he mixed up חלב with שומן and ate it, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away רבא's proof. It shows the משנה's words can be read in the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'שוגג על פיהם' is read as one connected phrase, there are no extra words, so nothing extra is included. The words even point the other way: only the man who relied on the ruling is exempt. So the משנה does not settle the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps. This opens a rejection that offers another way to read the source.
Liable (he must bring his own offering)

phrases.english: Perhaps one who acted by mistake on their word
is the one who is exempt,
but if he mixed up forbidden fat with permitted fat
and ate it, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא שׁוֹגֵג עַל פִּיהֶם הוּא דְּפָטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not decide the law.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The phrase can be read as one unit with no extra words. Read that way, it limits the exemption to the man who relied on the ruling.

steps.title: Other version: רבא tries to prove from the same words that the mix-up case is liable
steps.stepSummary: In the other version, רבא reads 'שוגג על פיהם' as one phrase. He tries to prove that only the man who relied on the ruling is exempt, so the man who mixed things up is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that רבא said: Come and hear. 'An individual went and acted by mistake on their word.' Doesn't this mean that only someone who acted by mistake because of their word is exempt? Then if he mixed up חלב with שומן and ate it, he would be liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the second version of רבא's words (step 18). This too is presented as an attempted proof, this time pointing to 'liable'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version uses the exact reading that was used to reject the first version. The phrase is one unit, so it only exempts the man who relied on the ruling. That would make the mix-up case liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that...? This opens a suggested proof.

phrases.english: Some say:
Rava said: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: הָלַךְ יָחִיד וְעָשָׂה שׁוֹגֵג עַל פִּיהֶם.
phrases.english: An individual went and acted by mistake on their word.
Is it not that one who acted by mistake on their word
is the one who is exempt,
but if he mixed up forbidden fat with permitted fat
and ate it, he is liable?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רָבָא, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This parallels step 20, but uses the second version of רבא's words (step 18).
steps.raayaObject: The man who mixed up חלב with שומן is liable.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's phrase 'שוגג על פיהם', read as one unit.

steps.title: Rejection: the משנה may mean either by mistake or on their word
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes the proof away. The phrase might list two separate cases: one who sinned by a mix-up, or one who relied on the ruling. Both are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it means either 'by mistake' or 'on their word'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second-version proof. It splits the phrase into two separate cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'שוגג' and 'על פיהם' are two different cases, then 'שוגג' covers the mix-up case, and that man is also exempt. So the משנה proves nothing in either direction. The next step shows that this case is an older dispute between רב and רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Either... or

steps.confusionAlert: This rejection does not say the mix-up man is liable. Both halves, 'by mistake' and 'on their word', are cases where he is exempt.
steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, the משנה's words can be read either way, so the משנה cannot settle רמי בר חמא's question. The next step shows that the case is already an older dispute between רב and רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: Perhaps:
either by mistake, or on their word.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא: אוֹ שׁוֹגֵג, אוֹ עַל פִּיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 22.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The phrase can be read as two separate cases, and both are exempt.

steps.title: The mix-up case is an older dispute between רב and רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this question was already argued about. רב says the man who mixed up חלב with שומן is exempt. רבי יוחנן says he is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is already a dispute. If the בית דין ruled that חלב is permitted, and someone mixed up חלב with שומן and ate it, רב says he is exempt and רבי יוחנן says he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the attempted proofs and tells us that earlier אמוראים already argued about this exact case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds he is exempt, because the court had permitted חלב anyway. רבי יוחנן holds he is liable, because he did not actually act because of the ruling. This dispute is the base for the challenge that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute (already argued by earlier sages)
Exempt

phrases.english: It is a dispute:
If the court ruled that forbidden fat is permitted,
and he mixed up forbidden fat with permitted fat and ate it:
Rav says: He is exempt,
and Rabbi Yochanan says: He is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּפְלוּגְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the attempted proofs failed, the גמרא shows the question is an older argument between אמוראים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the mix-up man is exempt. רבי יוחנן: he is liable.

steps.title: A ברייתא is brought against רבי יוחנן: a משומד is excluded
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a challenge against רבי יוחנן. It quotes a ברייתא that learns from the פסוק that a משומד does not bring a חטאת for a mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: The פסוק says 'from the common people, in his doing it'. This comes to exclude a משומד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing a ברייתא to challenge רבי יוחנן. This is the first part of a setup, and the actual attack comes in step 27.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא teaches that a משומד, who sins on purpose as a way of life, does not bring an offering even when he sins by mistake. The idea of excluding someone who would sin even if he knew will soon be used against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: An apostate, someone who rejects the מצוות
To exclude...

phrases.english: They challenged from a teaching:
"From the common people, in his doing it"
comes to exclude an apostate.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge to רבי יוחנן's view from step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן, who says the mix-up man is liable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא will set up a rule: only someone who would hold back if he knew brings an offering. Step 27 applies this rule to the mix-up man, who relied on the court and would not hold back, against רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: only one who would turn back if he knew brings an offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוסי, quoting רבי שמעון, learns the same rule from the words 'או הודע'. Someone who would turn back once he knew brings a קרבן, and someone who would not turn back does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יוסי says in the name of רבי שמעון: That is not needed, because the פסוק says, 'that should not be done, by mistake, and is guilty, or it becomes known to him.' One who would turn back because of his knowing brings an offering for his mistake. One who would not turn back because of his knowing does not bring an offering for his mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a second opinion that gives a wider rule. The גמרא is still setting up its challenge to רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets a test: a חטאת is only for someone who would have stopped if he had known the truth. The man in the mix-up case would have eaten the חלב anyway, since the court permitted it. So this rule seems to fit רב (exempt) and to work against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed (there is a better source)
One who would turn back because of his knowing
His mistaken sin
An offering (here, a חטאת)

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'שב מידיעתו' is the key idea. It tests whether the person's mistake is what really caused the sin, and the coming challenge to רבי יוחנן is built on it.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yosei says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
It is not needed,
since it says:
"that should not be done, by mistake,
and he is guilty, or it becomes known to him":
one who would turn back because of his knowing
brings an offering for his mistake.
One who would not turn back because of his knowing
does not bring an offering for his mistake.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 25 with a second opinion and a wider source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only someone who would turn back if he knew the truth brings a חטאת for his mistake.

steps.title: The man who mixed things up would never turn back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge against רבי יוחנן. The man who mixed up חלב with שומן would not regret his act even if he found out, so by the rule just learned he should be exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if this rule is true, isn't this man someone who would not turn back once he knew?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now finishes the challenge it started in step 25. It uses the rule from the פסוק to attack רבי יוחנן, who said the man who mixed things up is liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 25 and 26 taught that only someone who would turn back once he knew brings a חטאת. This man relied on the court's ruling that חלב is allowed, so even if he learned he ate חלב, he would not be sorry. That seems to make him exempt, which goes against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it is so (if this rule is true)
Someone who would not turn back once he knew

phrases.english: And if it is so,
phrases.notes: If the rule from step 26 is true, that only someone who would turn back brings a קרבן.

phrases.english: isn't this one who would not turn back even once he knew?
phrases.notes: This is the man who mixed up חלב with שומן. He relied on the court, so knowing the truth would not make him sorry.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אִיתָא, הָא לֹא שָׁב מִידִיעָתוֹ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from steps 25 and 26 to the case argued about in step 24, as a challenge against רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the man who mixed up חלב with שומן is liable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only someone who would turn back once he knew brings a חטאת. This man relied on the court and would not turn back, so he should be exempt.

steps.title: רב פפא: the man will turn back when the court does
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains רבי יוחנן. When the court finds out its mistake it will take back its ruling, and then this man will also be sorry. So he counts as someone who turns back, and he is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: רבי יוחנן holds that once the court finds out, it takes back its ruling, and this man also turns back. So we call him 'one who turns back once he knows,' and he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge against רבי יוחנן. He shows that the man does count as someone who would turn back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge said the man would never be sorry because he trusts the court. רב פפא says to look one step further: the court itself will fix its mistake once it learns the truth. When that happens, the man will be sorry too, so he fits the rule and must bring a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (this is his way of thinking)
The court
They take back (their ruling)
Liable (must bring a קרבן)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, the man who mixed up חלב with שומן is liable, because he will regret his act once the court takes back its ruling.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said,
Rabbi Yochanan holds:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּכִי מִתְיְדַע לְהוּ לְבֵי דִינָא,
phrases.english: since when it becomes known to the court,
phrases.notes: Known to the court that its ruling was a mistake.

phrases.english: they take back their ruling,
and he too turns back,
we call him 'one who turns back once he knows,' and he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, קָסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27 and defends רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the case differently: the man does count as one who would turn back.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the man trusts the court, he would never be sorry, so he should be exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the court will take back its ruling and he will follow, he counts as one who turns back, and he is liable.

steps.title: רבא: even רב agrees this man does not count toward the majority
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that even רב, who exempts the man who mixed things up, agrees that he does not count toward the majority of the community. The פסוק 'בשגגה' teaches that everyone must have sinned through the same kind of mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רב agrees that this man does not help make up the majority of the community. Why? The פסוק says 'by mistake,' which teaches that they must all have sinned through one and the same mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a new point about רב's opinion. He limits how far רב's ruling goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court brings its own קרבן only when most of the people sinned by its ruling. רב exempted the man who mixed things up, but that does not mean he counts as one of those people. The others made the mistake of trusting the ruling, while he mixed up two kinds of fat, so his mistake is a different one.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees (even the one who might be expected to disagree)

steps.title: Back to the משנה: why list all these cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's list: whether the judges sinned and he sinned with them, and so on. It asks why the משנה needed to list all these cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'Whether they did it and he did it with them, etc.' Why did the משנה need to teach all of these?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes the start of its list of cases. It asks why so many cases are needed, and this sets up the sharper challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists three cases: he sinned with the judges, after them, or alone. The גמרא wants to know why one case was not enough. The next step makes the question more exact.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה lists several cases instead of just one.

steps.title: The first part builds up, but the liability part should go the other way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the first part of the משנה makes sense, because it uses a 'not only this, but even that' style. But in the later part, where the man is liable, the order should be reversed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense in the first part, because it teaches 'not only this, but even that.' But the last part, which is about being liable, should have been taught the other way around!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens its question. The order of the list works for the exempt cases but seems backward for the liable cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first part, each case is a bigger step: he is exempt with the judges, and even after them, and even alone. That is a normal 'not only this, but even that' build-up. In the liability part, the build-up should start from the case where liability is most obvious, so the same order seems backward.

steps.kashyaTarget: The order of cases in the liability part of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A 'not only this, but even that' list must grow from the obvious case to the surprising one. That works for the exempt cases, but the liability cases should then be listed in reverse order.
